seoTitle: How to Issue a Partial Refund on eBay (2026)
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to issuing partial refunds on eBay for damaged items or buyer disputes, including how it affects fees and seller ratings.
intro: Not every buyer complaint needs a full return — a missing accessory, a small scuff, or a shipping delay is often best resolved by refunding part of the price and letting the buyer keep the item. That saves you return shipping, saves the buyer a second wait, and usually closes the issue faster than a formal case. This guide walks through where the partial refund tools actually live inside My eBay, then covers picking a reason, entering the amount, and following up with the buyer so the resolution sticks.

steps.heading: Open My eBay and head into Selling
steps.body: Everything starts from My eBay's Activity tab, the same dashboard that shows your offers, watchlist, and purchase history. The Selling section in the left-hand menu is what expands into the tools you actually need — it's easy to overlook if you're used to jumping straight to Seller Hub, but it works just as well and is the more direct route on a personal account. Sign in first if you land on eBay's create-account screen instead; that page only appears if your session has expired, so a quick re-login gets you back to the dashboard.

image.caption: My eBay's Activity dashboard with the Selling menu expanding in the left sidebar — the starting point before you can touch any order.

steps.heading: Find the order under Orders
steps.body: Once Selling is expanded, the full list of sub-sections appears: Overview, Sell an item, Drafts, Scheduled, Active, Orders, Unsold, Payments, and Shipping labels. Orders is the one you want — it's where every completed sale lives, searchable by buyer name or item title, and it's the same list a seller checks when relisting an unsold item or printing a shipping label. Click into the specific order tied to the buyer's complaint before doing anything else, since the refund tools are scoped to that individual transaction rather than being a general account setting.

image.caption: The full Selling sidebar, with Orders sitting between Active and Unsold — this is the real entry point for any refund.

steps.heading: Start the refund from the order details
steps.body: Inside an individual order, eBay gives you a "More actions" or "Issue a refund" option that opens the refund panel without cancelling the sale or starting a formal return. This is the key distinction from a standard return: the item stays sold, the buyer keeps it, and only money moves. Use this path when the buyer's issue is minor enough that shipping the item back and forth would cost more in time and postage than it's worth to either side.

steps.heading: Select the reason that matches the situation
steps.body: eBay asks for a reason before processing the refund — options like item not as described, buyer changed their mind, or a problem with the order cover most cases. Picking the accurate one matters because it's what eBay references if the buyer later opens a case, and it also determines whether your final value fee gets adjusted automatically. Don't default to the vaguest option just to move faster; a specific reason protects you if the same buyer disputes the transaction again later.

steps.heading: Enter the partial amount, not the full total
steps.body: The refund form lets you type any dollar figure up to the order total, so enter the partial amount you've agreed on rather than the full price. A common approach is refunding roughly what the missing part or defect is worth relative to the item — a cracked case on an otherwise-working phone might warrant 15-20% back, for example. Double-check the number before submitting, since eBay processes it immediately and there's no simple way to claw back an overpaid refund.

steps.heading: Message the buyer and confirm it landed
steps.body: Send a short message explaining what you refunded and why, ideally right after you submit it — buyers are far less likely to escalate to a formal case when they've already heard from you directly. The refund typically shows in the buyer's original payment method within a few business days, and you can track its status back in the same order view under Orders. If a buyer says they haven't seen it after a week, check the payment method on file before assuming something went wrong on eBay's end.

faq.question: Does a partial refund affect my eBay seller rating?
faq.answer: Handled promptly and communicated well, a partial refund is generally viewed favorably and can help you avoid a negative review or formal case.

faq.question: Are eBay fees adjusted after a partial refund?
faq.answer: eBay typically adjusts final value fees proportionally to the refunded amount, though the adjustment isn't always instant.

faq.question: Can a buyer request a partial refund themselves?
faq.answer: Buyers can message a seller requesting one, but only the seller can actually issue it through their order details — eBay doesn't let buyers self-serve a partial refund.

faq.question: Is a partial refund better than accepting a return?
faq.answer: For minor issues, a partial refund saves both parties the cost and hassle of return shipping, which is often preferable for low-value or bulky items.

faq.question: Where in My eBay do I find a specific order to refund?
faq.answer: Expand the Selling section in My eBay's left sidebar and click Orders — every completed sale is listed there, searchable by buyer or item title.
